messages:
maya: quick share — ran a KV-cache bench comparing H100 vs A100 across us/eu regions with int8 quantized LLM + prefetcher replay. saw unexpected p99 blowups in eu when seqlen distribution skews long.

nate: can you paste the p99 numbers? rough is fine.

maya: H100(us): p50=7ms, p95=18ms, p99=38ms; throughput ~120 req/s per GPU for batch=1 steady.
H100(eu): p50=8ms, p95=22ms, p99=82ms (this is the weird part).
A100(us): p50=9ms, p95=24ms, p99=70ms.
A100(eu): p50=10ms, p95=28ms, p99=95ms.

li: yikes. those eu p99s almost double. same model version & kernel?

sophia: were you using the adaptive eviction sweep or plain LRU?

maya: adaptive-hybrid eviction on H100, LRU on A100 for the first run, but I reproduced with both kernels. the big diff correlates with paging events (kv spillback) during long sequences.

nate: any chance it's a scheduler/capacity artifact in eu cluster? node mix?

maya: checked node mix — homogeneous h100s in that pool. noticed higher tail when the regional prefetcher replay window was conservative (small). bumping prefetch window from 8 -> 24 tokens reduced p99 by ~30% on H100(eu) but increased average GPU mem pressure.

sophia: tradeoff sounds classic: larger prefetch helps hitrate -> lower stall but ups memory and kernel eviction churn. did you try different quant kernels? int8 fastpath vs fp16 kernel selection?

maya: yes. int8 codepath saved ~15% throughput but increased cache-lookup latency slightly (more instructions per kv lookup). switching to fp16 kernel for hot kernel resulted in slightly better p99 but worse throughput.

perf-bot: [AUTO] perf regression detected for model redwood-v2-int8 in eu region: p99 +38% over baseline (trigger threshold 20%).

kubebot: deploy-note: rolled prefetch window tweak to canary (eu-serve-03) at 2245679000. monitor for 30m.

li: do we have the hitrate vs latency curve? that would help pick the sweet spot for prefetch window and eviction watermark.

maya: uploaded series to dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/kvbench/2245678910 — contains heatmaps (seqlen buckets: 8/32/128/512), hitrate vs p99 per region and kernel.

nate: quick config snippet you used?

maya: ```
# prefetch config (canary)
prefetch:
  window: 24
  max_concurrent_prefetch: 64
eviction:
  policy: hybrid_adaptive
  cold_watermark: 0.65
  hot_watermark: 0.9
kv_store:
  mode: persistent
  max_spillback_retries: 2
quant:
  prefer_kernel: int8_fastpath
```

li: thanks. one idea — add a transient replay buffer that keeps recent KV entries for 1s in local GPU mem to avoid immediate spillback during bursts. that might cut p99 without global memory increase.

sophia: also test a slightly higher cold_watermark (0.7) + evict-peek heuristic so we avoid flushing entries that are likely to be reaccessed in the next 50 tokens. small heuristic change reduced p99 by ~12% in earlier tests.

maya: will run those combos tomorrow with region-specific canaries. planning runs across seqlen mixes: chatty (8/32 heavy), longform (128/512 heavy), and mixed.

nate: please include kernel switch logs — we need to see when runtime flips kernels during long seqs (that correlates to spillback).

maya: will attach logs. ETA ~1800 UTC tomorrow. tagging @sophia @li @nate for follow-up. :eyes: :thumbsup:
